output.reason: A few days of right-hand numbness and tingling worse at night, with no reported weakness, facial droop or speech change, fits a typical nerve-compression pattern that can start with self-care guidance and a clear escalation trigger.
output.patientMessage: You can start self-care now: avoid bending your wrist while sleeping (a neutral wrist splint at night often helps), take breaks from repetitive hand use, and track which fingers are affected. Night-time hand numbness commonly comes from nerve compression at the wrist. If you develop hand weakness, dropping things, lasting loss of feeling, or sudden face droop, slurred speech or arm weakness, call 911.
differential: Carpal tunnel syndrome (median nerve compression at the wrist)
Other peripheral nerve compression, e.g. thoracic outlet or cervical origin
